planting.note: Plant fresh nuts in fall for natural cold stratification, or cold-moist stratify for 90-120 days and sow in spring, in deep, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Plant bare-root or container trees in deep, well-drained soil with a full sun exposure and ample room for a broad, spreading canopy. This California native walnut tolerates heavier soils, summer heat, and some drought better than English walnut, and was historically the dominant rootstock onto which commercial English walnut orchards in California were grafted. Left ungrafted, it produces a heavy crop of small, thick-shelled, strongly flavored nuts that are more work to crack than commercial walnuts but valued for wildlife forage and rootstock breeding.
sources: University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources

planting.note: Plant container-grown seedlings in spring in dry, rocky, or gravelly, very well-drained soil in full sun; established trees need little to no supplemental irrigation.

directions: Plant in dry, rocky, well-drained soil in full sun and avoid summer irrigation once established, since this California foothill native is adapted to long, hot, dry summers and thin, mineral soils. Gray pine has an open, sparse, gray-green crown and produces very large, heavy cones armed with hooked spines that contain large, oily, edible seeds long harvested by California Indigenous peoples as a staple food. It is one of the most drought-tolerant pines suitable for a nut crop and grows slowly but steadily on marginal sites unsuited to most other nut trees.
sources: USDA Forest Service Fire Effects Information System

planting.note: Plant container-grown seedlings in spring in dry, rocky, well-drained, neutral to alkaline soil in full sun; site where winters are cold and summers are dry.

directions: Plant in dry, well-drained, rocky soil in full sun on a site that mimics its native semi-arid mountain slopes of the northwestern Himalaya. Chilgoza pine is a slow-growing, long-lived five-needle pine with distinctive flaking, patchwork bark and is cultivated commercially in its native range for its large, thin-shelled, richly flavored pine nuts, among the most prized pine nuts in South and Central Asian cuisine. It requires cold winter dormancy and sharp drainage, and takes many years from planting to first significant cone production.
sources: Kew Plants of the World Online

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container-grown grafted trees in late winter to early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; a compatible pollenizer variety is required nearby.

directions: Plant grafted trees in deep, well-drained soil in full sun with a compatible pollenizer variety planted nearby, since Butte is not self-fertile. Butte is a mid-to-late blooming California commercial almond noted for its heavy, consistent bearing, semi-hard shell, and small, plump kernel, and it is frequently interplanted with Nonpareil as a reliable cross-pollinating partner. Its later bloom compared with Nonpareil reduces exposure to early spring frost damage in many California growing regions.
sources: UC Davis Fruit & Nut Research and Information Center

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container-grown grafted trees in late winter to early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; a single tree can set a crop without a separate pollenizer.

directions: Plant grafted trees in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; unlike most almond cultivars, Independence is self-fertile and can produce a good crop as a solid block planting without a separate pollenizer variety or heavy reliance on pollinator bees during bloom. It produces a semi-hard shell nut comparable in size and quality to Nonpareil, blooms later than many traditional varieties, and has become popular with growers seeking to reduce pollination costs and frost risk.
sources: UC Davis Fruit & Nut Research and Information Center
University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container-grown grafted trees in late winter to early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun with room for a large canopy.

directions: Plant grafted trees in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, allowing enough room for a large, vigorous, spreading canopy. Hartley is a long-established English walnut variety recognized for its large, elongated, smooth-shelled nuts and light-colored, mild-flavored kernel, and it was for decades a mainstay of California commercial walnut orchards. It has been largely replaced in new plantings by more disease-tolerant modern varieties, but mature Hartley trees remain productive and are still valued for nut size and quality in older orchards and home gardens.
sources: UC Davis Fruit & Nut Research and Information Center

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container-grown grafted trees in late winter to early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Plant grafted trees in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, spacing them to accommodate the tree's naturally compact, spreading form. Howard is a widely planted California commercial English walnut variety valued for its lateral bearing habit, which sets nuts along the length of each branch rather than only at the tips, boosting yields per acre. It produces a light-colored, high-quality kernel and buds out later than older varieties such as Hartley, reducing the risk of spring frost damage to the crop.
sources: UC Davis Fruit & Nut Research and Information Center

planting.note: Plant fresh nuts or container-grown seedlings in spring after cold-moist stratification, in well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to light shade.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to light shade, giving the tree room to develop its narrower, more elongated leaves than other chestnut species. Native to central and southern China, Chinese chinkapin is a distinct chestnut species from Castanea mollissima, bearing small burs that typically enclose a single sweet nut rather than the two or three found in most chestnuts. It has been used by breeders exploring additional sources of blight tolerance and is planted both as a nut producer and as an ornamental shade tree in its native range.
sources: Kew Plants of the World Online

common_name: Tonda Gentile delle Langhe Hazelnut (Piedmont Hazelnut)

planting.note: Plant container-grown or bare-root shrubs in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; a compatible pollenizer hazelnut is needed for reliable nut set.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun and provide a compatible pollenizer variety nearby, since this hazelnut is not self-fertile. Tonda Gentile delle Langhe is the classic hazelnut of Italy's Piedmont region, celebrated for its round shape, thin shell, and rich, sweet, highly aromatic kernel that is the traditional standard for fine chocolate-hazelnut confections. Like most European hazelnut cultivars it is quite susceptible to eastern filbert blight in humid North American climates, so it performs best in drier growing regions or where the disease pressure is low.

planting.note: Plant bare-root or container seedlings in early spring; red hickory develops a deep taproot and resists transplanting once established, so site it carefully.

directions: Plant seedlings in deep, well-drained upland soil in full sun, allowing room for a tall, straight-trunked tree. Red hickory is a native eastern North American species closely related to pignut hickory, distinguished by its reddish twigs and a husk that splits more readily and completely from the nut at maturity. Its kernels are notably sweeter and less bitter than those of true pignut hickory, and the tree is a valuable wildlife mast producer as well as a source of dense, strong wood.

planting.note: Plant fresh nuts in fall for natural stratification, or cold-moist stratify for 90-120 days and plant grafted or seedling trees in spring, in deep, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Plant in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, siting two or more trees for reliable pollination. Buartnut is a naturally occurring and cultivated hybrid between butternut (Juglans cinerea) and Japanese walnut or heartnut (Juglans ailantifolia), combining some of butternut's rich, oily flavor with heartnut's heavier and more reliable nut production. Because true butternut has been decimated across its range by butternut canker disease, buartnut is grown by nut enthusiasts in colder climates as a hardier, often more disease-tolerant alternative that still carries much of the butternut flavor profile.

planting.note: Direct sow nuts in fall for spring germination after natural cold stratification, or cold-moist stratify for 90-120 days and sow in early spring.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun, allowing the shrub to form its natural dense, multi-stemmed thicket. Asian hazel is native to Siberia, Korea, northern China, and Japan and is exceptionally cold hardy compared with the European hazelnut, tolerating harsh continental winters that would damage most commercial filbert cultivars. It produces small nuts in short, bristly husks and is widely used by breeders working to develop cold-hardy, blight-resistant hazelnut cultivars for the northern United States and Canada by crossing it with European hazelnut.
sources: Rutgers New Jersey Agricultural Experiment Station
